items.title: Ornith-1.0-9B and Ornith-1.0-35B models now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
items.summary:
DeepReinforce AI's Ornith-1.0-9B and Ornith-1.0-35B models are now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, expanding the portfolio of foundation models available to AWS customers. These two models are part of the Ornith 1.0 family of open-source, self-scaffolding agentic coding models released under the MIT license, achieving state-of-the-art performance among open-source models of comparable size on coding benchmarks such as Terminal-Bench 2.1, SWE-Bench, NL2Repo, and OpenClaw.
 
These models address different agentic coding challenges with specialized capabilities:
 
Ornith-1.0-9B is a lightweight 9B-parameter dense model post-trained on Qwen 3.5 9B, designed for efficient single-GPU deployment. With a 256K-token context window and 32 decoder layers, it is well-suited for individual developers and small teams running agentic coding workflows on a single GPU — including laptops with consumer-grade hardware. Its self-improving training framework uses reinforcement learning to jointly optimize scaffold generation and solution rollouts, enabling the model to discover better search trajectories and generate higher-quality code solutions.
 
Ornith-1.0-35B is a 35B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) model post-trained on Qwen 3.5, delivering stronger agentic coding performance while remaining deployable on a single 24GB consumer GPU. Like its smaller sibling, it employs reinforcement learning to jointly optimize the scaffolds that drive coding tasks and the resulting solution rollouts, discovering superior code trajectories. Its MoE architecture activates only a subset of parameters per token, providing a strong balance of quality and efficiency for production agentic coding workloads.
 
With SageMaker JumpStart, customers can deploy any of these models with just a few clicks to address their specific AI use cases.
 
To get started with these models, navigate to the SageMaker JumpStart model catalog in the SageMaker console or use the SageMaker Python SDK to deploy the models to your AWS account. For more information about deploying and using foundation models in SageMaker JumpStart, see the Amazon SageMaker JumpStart documentation.

items.title: DeepSeek-V4-Pro, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash models now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart
items.summary:
DeepSeek's DeepSeek-V4-Pro, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash models are now available on Amazon SageMaker JumpStart, expanding the portfolio of foundation models available to AWS customers. These three open-weight Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) language models, released under the MIT license, deliver frontier-class performance across reasoning, coding, and agentic workloads while activating only a fraction of their total parameters per token, enabling high efficiency at scale.
 
These models address different AI challenges with specialized capabilities:
 
DeepSeek-V4-Pro is designed for complex reasoning and high-quality text generation at flagship scale. This 1.6T-parameter MoE model activates 49B parameters per token and supports a 1M-token context window, making it well-suited for long-document analysis, multi-step reasoning, and demanding generation tasks that require maximum model capacity.
 
DeepSeek-V4-Flash delivers strong performance at significantly lower compute cost as an efficient 284B-parameter MoE model activating 13B parameters per token. It supports the same 1M-token context window as V4-Pro, making it ideal for latency-sensitive and cost-conscious production deployments across a wide range of language tasks.
 
DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash provides next-generation agentic efficiency with native multimodal support. Built on a novel Causal Encoder-Decoder (CED) architecture with a 552B-parameter backbone, it activates just 8B parameters during prefill and 16B during decode, supporting a 1M-token context window and 384K max output tokens. Its Compressed Sparse Attention 2 (CSA2) and FP4 KV caching reduce the global KV cache footprint to roughly 1/4 of V4-Flash, delivering substantially improved cost efficiency for agentic workloads, coding, and vision tasks.
 
With SageMaker JumpStart, customers can deploy any of these models with just a few clicks to address their specific AI use cases.
 
To get started with these models, navigate to the SageMaker JumpStart model catalog in the SageMaker console or use the SageMaker Python SDK to deploy the models to your AWS account. For more information about deploying and using foundation models in SageMaker JumpStart, see the Amazon SageMaker JumpStart documentation.

items.title: AWS Cloud WAN now supports Flow Logs
items.summary:
AWS Cloud WAN now supports VPC Flow Logs, giving you central visibility into IP traffic across your global network. Flow Logs capture detailed information for each flow, so you can understand how traffic moves across your core network without leaving your AWS Cloud WAN account.
 
Until now, network administrators had to stitch together VPC Flow Logs from many VPCs, accounts, and Regions to see traffic across their global network. They often depended on other teams for access to those logs. Cloud WAN Flow Logs give core network owners one consolidated view of traffic between VPCs, Regions, and on-premises networks connected over AWS Direct Connect, AWS Site-to-Site VPN, or SD-WAN. You can use this data to troubleshoot connectivity and performance problems, plan capacity from historical bandwidth trends, find unusual traffic patterns, and keep records for security and compliance. Flow log records include IP addresses, ports, protocol, traffic volume, and packet-loss counters, along with Cloud WAN metadata such as segment, Region, service insertion hops and attachment details. You can turn on Flow Logs for an entire core network, a single core network edge, or individual attachments. You can publish them to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), or Amazon Data Firehose. Cloud WAN adds no charge for Flow Logs. Standard charges apply for each destination.
 
Cloud WAN Flow Logs are available in all AWS Regions where AWS Cloud WAN is available. You can get started with the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, or API. To learn more, see AWS Cloud WAN Flow Logs user guide.

items.title: Amazon EKS Provisioned Control Plane now offers a 24 GB etcd database on 4XL and 8XL tiers
items.summary:
Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) now offers a larger 24 GB etcd database, up from 16 GB, for 4XL and 8XL Provisioned Control Plane clusters. etcd is the key-value store in the Kubernetes control plane that holds your cluster state, so its size limits how many Kubernetes objects your cluster can store. With 50% more capacity, you can run bigger clusters with more pods, jobs, events, and custom resources.
 
The larger database gives more headroom to workloads that create and update many Kubernetes objects, such as large-scale AI/ML training and inference, batch processing, and CI/CD pipelines. When the etcd database fills up, you can’t add or change objects in your cluster, so the extra headroom helps keep these workloads running as they scale.
 
To get the larger database, choose the 4XL or 8XL tier of Provisioned Control Plane on a cluster running EKS version 1.34 or later. Existing clusters on the 4XL and 8XL tiers running these versions get the larger database automatically, with no action required. The 24 GB etcd database is available in all commercial AWS Regions where Provisioned Control Plane is available. To learn more, see the Amazon EKS Provisioned Control Plane user guide.

items.summary: AWS Emulator is a free, open-source local emulator in Rust that lets developers test applications against nearly every AWS service on their own machine using the same CLI and SDK commands, with fidelity measured against real AWS behavior.

items.title: Amazon Cognito now supports user pool session management
items.summary:
Amazon Cognito now supports session management for user pools, giving you visibility into and control over the sessions your users establish when they sign in to your applications. Single sign-on (SSO) sessions are created when a user signs in through managed login and let them access other app clients without re-authenticating. Token sessions are created when a user signs in to an app client and receives tokens. Session management lets you list a user's active SSO and token sessions across all devices and app clients and revoke any of them on demand. You can also now configure how long each app client reuses an SSO session before requiring re-authentication, instead of the previous fixed one-hour duration.
 
Each session includes details such as session type, app client ID, device type, last activity time and location, and initial sign-in time, so you can build your own end-user or admin session experiences. You can revoke an individual session, optionally with its linked sessions, or use global sign-out to end all sessions associated with one user. You can also set a maximum number of active token sessions per user.
 
Session management is available for user pools in the Essentials or Plus feature plans in all AWS Regions where Amazon Cognito is available. You can manage sessions using the AWS Management Console, API, AWS Command Line Interface, and AWS Software Development Kits, and configure settings with AWS CloudFormation. Visit the Developer Guide and API Reference for details.

items.title: AWS Lambda MicroVMs now supports the x86 CPU architecture
items.summary:
AWS Lambda MicroVMs now supports the x86 CPU architecture, so you can run your existing x86 applications, tools, and software dependencies without recompiling or porting them. When you create a MicroVM image, you can now choose between x86 and Arm (AWS Graviton) to give each user or job an isolated MicroVM on the architecture your workload uses.
 
Lambda MicroVMs is a serverless compute primitive that provides VM-level isolation, near-instant launch and resume, and state preservation for running user or AI-generated code, in applications such as AI coding assistants, CI/CD runners, interactive development environments, and vulnerability scanners. Today’s launch enables you to run x86-based workloads on Lambda MicroVMs as-is. For workloads that run on Arm, you can continue using AWS Graviton processors which is the default CPU architecture option.
 
To start building x86 workloads on Lambda MicroVMs, choose the x86 architecture when you create a MicroVM image from your Dockerfile, then launch MicroVMs from that image. You can use MicroVMs through the AWS Lambda console, AWS CloudFormation, AWS Cloud Development Kit, or with your preferred agentic development tools using the Agent Toolkit for AWS.
 
Support for the x86 CPU architecture is available in all AWS Regions where Lambda MicroVMs is available, except Asia Pacific (Hong Kong), Asia Pacific (Malaysia), Asia Pacific (Thailand), and Europe (Spain). To learn more, visit the AWS Lambda MicroVMs developer guide. For information on pricing, see Lambda MicroVMs pricing.

items.title: Amazon EKS Auto Mode now supports security groups for Pods
items.summary:
Amazon EKS Auto Mode now supports security groups for Pods, letting you apply dedicated Amazon EC2 security group rules to individual Pods. Different workloads on the same node can carry different security groups, giving your Pods network-level segmentation without creating separate node pools for each application.
 
Security groups for Pods extends your existing AWS network controls to the Pod level, so your Pods can reach resources such as Amazon RDS and Amazon ElastiCache databases that authorize connections by security group under the same rules the rest of your VPC uses. You define which Pods receive which security groups with a SecurityGroupPolicy resource, and Pods not matched by a policy keep using their node’s security groups.
 
Security groups for Pods is included as part of EKS Auto Mode at no additional charge and is available on clusters running Kubernetes version 1.36 or later, in all AWS Regions where EKS Auto Mode is supported. To learn more, see Security groups for Pods in the Amazon EKS User Guide and the Amazon EKS Auto Mode product page.

items.title: AWS Emulator is now available for building and testing AWS applications locally
items.summary:
AWS Emulator is now available for building and testing AWS applications locally.
 
Starting today, you can use AWS Emulator to build and test AWS applications on your computer or in your continuous integration (CI) environment. Your existing AWS SDK and CLI calls go to AWS Emulator and come back in milliseconds, so you and your coding agents can find and fix errors locally, with no deployments or AWS account required.
 
You create and manage resources with the same AWS SDK and AWS CLI calls you use with AWS, signed with credentials the emulator provides. For the operations it supports, AWS Emulator returns the same result as AWS for valid calls and the same errors for invalid ones. Operations it doesn’t yet support return 501 Not Implemented. AWS Emulator keeps the state of your resources in memory until you stop it. Each copy you start gets its own port, keys and in-memory state, so agents, test suites, and CI jobs never see each other’s resources. For example, a coding agent can create an Amazon DynamoDB table, test against it offline, and fix its code before it deploys.
 
Services in AWS Emulator are generated from the API models AWS publishes, the same models behind the AWS SDKs. When AWS adds a service or API, it shows up in AWS Emulator, and its behavior is filled in and verified release by release. To see how its responses compare to AWS, review the AWS Emulator fidelity report.
 
AWS Emulator doesn’t depend on an AWS Region. AWS Emulator has no additional service fee. You pay only for AWS resources when you deploy to AWS. Its source code is published under the CC0 1.0 Universal public domain dedication. To get started, see the AWS Emulator documentation, or view the source in the AWS Emulator GitHub repository.

items.title: AWS Quick apps are now available in Asia Pacific (Singapore)
items.summary:
The AWS Quick desktop app for macOS and Windows and the Quick mobile app for iOS and Android are now available in the Asia Pacific (Singapore) Region. This launch builds on the recent availability of Quick in Singapore.
 
The desktop app works with your local files and connects to your calendar, email, and business apps. The mobile app lets you chat with Quick, review your activity feed, and open dashboards. Your conversations, context, and agents stay in sync across web, desktop, and mobile, so you can start an agent on your desktop, check on it from your phone, and let it keep running after you close your computer. 
 
To get started, download the desktop app from the AWS Quick download page or the mobile app from the Apple App Store or Google Play. To learn more, see AWS Quick on mobile in the AWS Quick User Guide and the AWS Quick product page.

items.title: Amazon SES now supports higher limits for email identities, tenants, and configuration sets
items.summary:
Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) now supports higher limits for email identities, tenants, and configuration sets. You can view your current usage against each limit and request increases in the AWS Service Quotas console. A single account can now keep pace with your growth, so you no longer need to split email workloads across several accounts to stay within per-account limits.
 
Customers running multi-tenant workloads often create a separate email identity, tenant, or configuration set for each customer, brand, or AI agent they serve. As you add more customers, brands, and AI agents, these resources can multiply quickly, and higher limits let all of these workloads grow in one account. To help you manage larger accounts, you can now also search these resources by name or status.
 
Higher limits for email identities, tenants, and configuration sets are available in all AWS Regions where Amazon SES is available.
 
To learn more, see Service quotas in Amazon SES in the Amazon SES Developer Guide and the Amazon SES product page.

items.title: AWS Billing and Cost Management now supports AWS Billing Conductor and AWS Billing Transfer views as source views for custom billing views
items.summary:
Custom billing views now support AWS Billing Conductor and AWS Billing Transfer views as source views. These are the views AWS maintains per billing group and per billing transfer relationship. You can combine them into a single custom billing view, apply filters, and use that view in Cost Explorer, AWS Budgets, and the Billing and Cost Management console. There are three source view types. Billing group views contain the cost of each Billing Conductor billing group, which you can combine for chargeback and showback across business units. Billing transfer views contain the cost transferred to you for each end customer, and transfer showback views contain the cost that end customer sees. Aggregating each type gives you your total transferred cost and the total bill your end customers see.
 
Your access does not change: you can use an AWS-managed view as a source only where you can already access it. Once created, you can share a custom billing view using AWS Resource Access Manager with accounts inside or outside your organization, so your finance team or a downstream seller works with the data in their own account. Whether you are an AWS Partner reselling AWS services or an organization using billing groups for pro forma billing, you get one consolidated view instead of one per customer or group.
 
This feature is available in all commercial AWS Regions at no additional cost. To get started, navigate to Billing Views in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console or view the user guide.

items.title: Amazon EC2 G7 instances now available in additional regions
items.summary:
Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) G7 instances powered by NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs are now available in Europe (London), Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Sydney) and South America (Sao Paulo) Regions. G7 instances deliver up to 4.6x AI inference performance and up to 2.1 graphics performance compared to G6 instances. G7 instances also deliver faster performance for GPU-accelerated data analytics workloads.
 
Customers can use G7 instances for deploying AI models for language translation, video and image analysis, speech recognition and recommender systems. They also accelerate graphics workloads such as creating and rendering real-time, cinematic-quality graphics and game streaming. Additionally, G7 instances support video transcoding, spatial computing, and data analytics workloads. G7 instances feature up to 8 NVIDIA RTX PRO 4500 Blackwell Server Edition GPUs with 32 GB of memory per GPU and custom Intel Xeon 6 processors. They support up to 192 virtual CPUs (vCPUs) and up to 700 Gbps of Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) networking bandwidth. They also support up to 768 GiB of system memory, and up to 7.6 TB of local NVMe SSD storage.
 
You can use G7 instances for Amazon EC2 in the following AWS Regions: US West (Oregon), US East (N. Virginia, Ohio) , Europe (London, Spain, Frankfurt, Stockholm) , Asia Pacific (Mumbai, Sydney) and South America (Sao Paulo). You can purchase G7 instances as On-Demand Instances, Spot Instances, or as part of Savings Plans.
 
To get started, visit the AWS Management Console, AWS Command Line Interface (CLI), and AWS SDKs. To learn more, visit the G7 instance page.

items.title: Amazon OpenSearch Service announces managed cross-Region disaster recovery
items.summary:
Amazon OpenSearch Service now offers managed cross-Region disaster recovery, so you can meet strict availability and business continuity requirements for mission-critical search, AI, and analytics workloads without building or maintaining replication yourself. After you create domains in two Regions, you can pair them with a single API call or a few steps in the AWS Management Console.
 
Managed disaster recovery delivers a recovery point objective (RPO) of under one minute and a recovery time objective (RTO) of under 20 minutes. The secondary domain stays continuously in sync with the primary. For planned events such as maintenance or Region rotation, a switchover swaps the two domains' roles with zero data loss. If your primary domain becomes unavailable, a failover promotes the secondary, with data loss limited to the replication lag. After a failover, you restore protection by pairing the new primary with a secondary domain. You can monitor replication health and lag with Amazon CloudWatch metrics.
 
Managed disaster recovery requires OpenSearch 3.7 or later and supports domains in the same AWS account, including domains encrypted with customer managed AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys. Domains that use UltraWarm storage or OpenSearch Optimized instances (OR1 or OR2) aren't supported. If you're on an earlier version, clone-based upgrades let you test OpenSearch 3.7 against your workload, cut over when you're ready, and roll back if needed.
 
There's no additional charge for managed disaster recovery. You pay standard rates for the secondary domain and cross-Region data transfer. For details, see Amazon OpenSearch Service pricing.
 
Managed disaster recovery is available today in all commercial AWS Regions where Amazon OpenSearch Service is available (Region list). To get started, see the disaster recovery documentation.

items.title: Amazon RDS for MySQL 26.10 is now available in Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment
items.summary:
Starting today, Amazon RDS for MySQL 26.10 is available in the Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment, allowing you to evaluate the pre-release of MySQL 26.10 on Amazon RDS for MySQL.
 
MySQL 26.10 includes bug fixes, security patches, and some improvements to READ COMMITTED workload performance and purge lag warnings in the error log. On busy READ COMMITTED workloads, NUMA systems performance could be impacted as each read view that closed required a global mutex. Read-view objects can now be reused which eliminates the global mutex on closure. The error log now reports warnings when the history-list length (HLL) crosses innodb_max_purge_lag and when purge lag begins delaying DML, so you can detect purge backlogs before they affect performance. To learn more, please refer to the MySQL 26.10 release notes.
 
Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment database instances are retained for a maximum period of 60 days and are automatically deleted after the retention period. Amazon RDS database snapshots that are created in the Preview Environment can only be used to create or restore database instances within the Preview Environment. Amazon RDS Database Preview Environment database instances are priced as per the pricing in the US East (Ohio) Region.

items.title: Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL announces Extended Support minor versions 13.23-rds.20260819, 12.22-rds.20260820 and 11.22-rds.20260822
items.summary:
Amazon Relational Database Service (RDS) for PostgreSQL announces Amazon RDS Extended Support minor versions 13.23-rds.20260819, 12.22-rds.20260820 and 11.22-rds.20260822.
 
Amazon RDS Extended Support provides up to three additional years of fixes for critical Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures (CVE) and bugs beyond a major version's end of standard support date, giving you more time to upgrade to a new major version.
 
You can upgrade your database using Amazon RDS Blue/Green Deployments, in-place upgrade, or restore from a snapshot. Learn more about performing version upgrades in the Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL User Guide.
 
Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL makes it simple to set up, operate, and scale PostgreSQL deployments in the cloud. Create or update a fully managed Amazon RDS database in the Amazon RDS Management Console or by using the AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI).

items.title: AWS Partner Central now provides an improved business planning experience
items.summary:
AWS Partner Central now offers a new business planning experience in the AWS Console. AWS Partners can initiate plans for growing their AWS business or collaborate on plans initiated by AWS teams.
 
Partners can collaborate with AWS partner development, technology, marketing, and specialist teams to define plan narratives, goals, and initiatives. AI-assisted plan readiness scores help partners identify areas to improve, while real-time tracking shows progress against goals. Partners can also add attachments and export plans to prepare for business reviews.
 
Partners can use application programming interfaces (APIs) and software development kits (SDKs) to integrate business planning into their workflows. Programmatic notifications are also available.
 
Business planning is available to AWS Partners who are actively engaged with AWS Partner management teams. AWS Partner Central is available in the US East (N. Virginia) Region. To get started, sign in to AWS Partner Central and choose Business Plan.

items.title: Amazon S3 Access Grants now support listing grants across multiple AWS accounts
items.summary:
Amazon S3 Access Grants can now discover and list all your grants across multiple AWS accounts with a single API call, eliminating the need to query each account separately. A single ListCallerAccessGrants call returns grants from your own S3 Access Grants instance and every instance shared with you, giving you a complete view of the S3 data you can access.
 
By setting the new InstanceScope parameter to ALL in your ListCallerAccessGrants request, S3 Access Grants queries every instance shared with you through AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) and returns all the grants in one combined response, each identifying the account that owns it. Additionally, when you request credentials with GetDataAccess for an S3 path and set InstanceScope to ALL, S3 Access Grants locates the owning account for you, routes the request to its instance, and returns credentials for the matching grant.
 
This capability is now available in all AWS Regions where S3 Access Grants is available, at no additional cost. You can use the AWS SDK, API, or CLI to list and access grants across accounts. To learn more, visit the S3 Access Grants overview page and the S3 documentation.

items.title: Amazon Bedrock adds bedrock-runtime endpoint support for Daybreak models
items.summary:
Eligible customers can now access OpenAI’s specialized cybersecurity models Daybreak Red: GPT-5.6 Cyber and Daybreak Blue: GPT-5.6 Sol through the bedrock-runtime endpoint on Amazon Bedrock.
  Daybreak Blue is the starting point for most security teams across defensive workflows, including vulnerability discovery, detection engineering, and incident response. Daybreak Red is designed for advanced, authorized tasks such as vulnerability research, exploit reproduction, and mitigation development. For these tasks, a lower refusal threshold, matched by stronger identity verification, monitoring, and access controls, improves the speed and depth of an investigation. Your inference data is not used for model training, and neither model requires you to opt in to sharing your data with OpenAI.
  On the bedrock-runtime endpoint, the models are available through US and Global cross-Region inference (CRIS) profiles. Access to the models requires enrollment in Daybreak access from OpenAI. To enroll, contact OpenAI or reach out to your AWS account team for guidance on eligibility. Once approved, work with your account team to request access on AWS. For regional availability through the bedrock-mantle endpoint and more information, view the documentation.

items.title: Amazon S3 Tables now support S3 server access logging
items.summary:
Amazon S3 Tables now support server access logging, providing you detailed records of the requests made to your table buckets. You can now track table operations, namespace management, and data access to support security audits, access analysis, and cost attribution. Log delivery is available at no additional cost, and you pay only for the storage of the log files.
 
When you enable server access logging on a table bucket, S3 delivers logs for requests to all tables and namespaces in that bucket to a general purpose bucket in the same account and Region. Each record captures the requester, operation, table name, namespace, response status, and request timing, using the same space-delimited format as S3 server access logs for general purpose buckets. This lets you reuse your existing log analysis workflows to query S3 Table logs with any query engine of your choice such as Amazon Athena and DuckDB.
 
Server access logging for S3 Tables is available in all AWS Regions where S3 Tables are available. You can enable it using the AWS Management Console, AWS CLI, AWS SDKs, or AWS CloudFormation. To learn more, visit the S3 Tables overview page and S3 Tables server access logging in the Amazon S3 User Guide.

items.title: AWS Marketplace SaaS free trials now convert automatically to paid subscriptions
items.summary:
Today, AWS Marketplace announces that free trials of usage-based software as a service (SaaS) products can now convert automatically to paid subscriptions. When a free trial ends, the buyer's subscription continues at the seller's usage-based pricing, so buyers pay only for what they use after the trial. This helps sellers turn more trial users into paying customers. Buyers get a simple way to evaluate software before they buy, with no new subscription and no interruption in access.
 
Sellers can offer a free trial of 7 to 90 days that converts to a paid subscription at the price they set. For example, a data team can try an analytics product for 30 days and, if it meets their needs, keep using it after the trial ends. Buyers see the trial length, conversion date, and pricing before they subscribe. They receive reminder emails before the trial converts and can cancel at any time before conversion at no charge.
 
Sellers can create a free trial in AWS Partner Central, or update an existing free trial offer to convert automatically. This capability is available for public offers in all AWS Regions where AWS Marketplace is available.
 
To learn more, see the AWS Marketplace Seller Guide and the AWS Marketplace Buyer Guide.

items.title: AWS Network Firewall launches next-generation firewall policy
items.summary:
Today, AWS announces next-generation firewall (NGFW) policy for AWS Network Firewall, a new policy model that provides security teams with a simpler policy structure and increased rule capacity. AWS Network Firewall is a managed network security service that protects your Amazon VPCs with access control and threat detection.
The new policy model strengthens your security posture by layering firewall and IPS protections instead of combining them, which also makes policies easier to manage. You author firewall rules that enforce deny-by-default access control, such as allowing traffic only to approved domains. For IPS rules, you can use managed rule groups from AWS or AWS Marketplace partners, which update automatically as new threats emerge. You can also create your own custom IPS rule groups. Firewall and IPS rules each have their own capacity, so you no longer trade one off against the other. For rules you don't share across policies, you can create embedded rule groups that draw capacity on demand without pre-allocation. With NGFW policy, all rules are stateful and evaluate with full connection context, for consistent, predictable traffic handling. Your existing policies continue to operate without changes, and IPS rules remain backward compatible.
NGFW policy is available at no additional charge in all commercial AWS Regions and AWS GovCloud (US) Regions. For a full list of supported regions, visit the AWS Capabilities by Region page.
To learn more, see the AWS Network Firewall product page and documentation.
